'''Armed conflicts and attacks''' 
*[[Gaza war]]
**[[Israeli invasion of the Gaza Strip]]
***Three [[Israeli Ground Forces|Israeli soldiers]] from the [[Givati Brigade]] are killed by an [[Improvised explosive device|IED explosion]] in [[Jabalia]], [[North Gaza Governorate]], during clashes with [[Hamas]] militants. [https://www.timesofisrael.com/three-idf-soldiers-killed-by-roadside-bomb-in-north-gazas-jabalia/ (''The Times of Israel'')]
**[[Rafah aid distribution incidents]]
***At least 27 [[Palestinians]] are killed by [[Israel Defense Forces|Israeli forces]] near an [[humanitarian aid|aid distribution]] centre in [[Rafah]], [[Gaza Strip|Gaza]]. [https://apnews.com/article/israel-palestinians-hamas-war-news-hostages-aid-06-03-2025-24ce3d395c7058362e650f2330a6476f (AP)] [https://www.reuters.com/world/middle-east/least-24-palestinians-killed-near-gaza-aid-site-medics-say-2025-06-03/ (Reuters)]
*[[Russian invasion of Ukraine]]
**[[2025 Crimean Bridge explosion]]
***The [[Crimean Bridge]] is temporarily closed and subsequently reopened by [[Russia]]n authorities after several underwater [[C-4 (explosive)|C-4 explosives]] planted under the bridge detonated. The [[Security Service of Ukraine]] claims responsibility, saying its agents planted 1.1 [[TNT equivalent|tonnes of TNT equivalent]] at a support section of the bridge. [https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/live/cr58e9yr2ezt (BBC News)]
**[[Attacks on civilians in the Russian invasion of Ukraine]]
***Four people are killed and 25 others are injured after [[Russian Armed Forces|Russian forces]] launch an [[Multiple rocket launcher|MLRS rocket]] barrage at the centre of [[Sumy]], [[Ukraine]]. [https://apnews.com/article/russia-ukraine-sumy-attack-zelenskyy-a6a513e388768e1d5179498302945bd3 (AP)]
*[[Allied Democratic Forces insurgency]]
**Two people, including a [[suicide bombing|suicide bomber]], are killed near a [[Roman Catholic]] shrine in [[Kampala]], [[Uganda]], on [[Uganda Martyrs|Uganda]] [[Martyrs' Day#Uganda|Martyrs' Day]]. [[Uganda Police Force|Police]] attribute the bombing to [[Allied Democratic Forces]] rebels. [https://www.reuters.com/business/media-telecom/explosion-reported-near-catholic-shrine-ugandas-capital-2025-06-03/ (Reuters)]
*[[Sudanese civil war (2023–present)|Sudanese civil war]]
**Five [[humanitarian aid|aid workers]] are killed in an attack on a 15-vehicle convoy delivering food to families in the [[Darfur region]], [[Sudan]]. The [[Sudanese Armed Forces]] and the [[Rapid Support Forces]] blame each other for the attack. [https://www.dw.com/en/sudan-5-killed-in-attack-on-aid-convoy-un-says/a-72781173 (DW)]

'''Arts and culture'''
*[[CJ Opiaza]] is officially crowned as [[Miss Grand International 2024]] following [[Rachel Gupta]]'s resignation and termination from the title. [https://www.abs-cbn.com/lifestyle/2025/6/3/-this-is-my-golden-moment-cj-opiaza-in-tears-at-miss-grand-international-coronation-1626 (ABS-CBN News)]

'''Disasters and accidents'''
*A [[bus]] crash kills eleven people and injures 17 others in [[Hualahuises]], [[Nuevo León]], [[Mexico]]. [https://www.reuters.com/world/americas/bus-accident-leaves-11-dead-17-injured-mexican-state-nuevo-leon-2025-06-03/ (Reuters)]
*[[Cessna Citation I]] is reported missing after takeoff from [[Simón Bolívar International Airport (Venezuela)|Simón Bolívar International Airport]] in [[Maiquetía]], Venezuela. On June 4, authorities reported finding remains of the aircraft including documents from inside the aircraft. It was revealed that 5 people were onboard instead of the previously reported 3. All onboard are presumed dead. [https://notiprensadigital.com/extraoficial-encuentran-restos-de-aeronave-desaparecida-tras-salir-de-maiquetia/ (Notiprensa Digital)]

'''International relations'''
*[[Brazil–United States relations]]
**[[Brazil]]ian [[President of Brazil|president]] [[Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva]] says that he will defend [[Supreme Court of Brazil|Supreme Court]] chief [[Alexandre de Moraes]] from potential U.S. [[International sanctions|sanctions]], which [[U.S. Secretary of State]] [[Marco Rubio]] threatened over the ongoing trial of former Brazilian president [[Jair Bolsonaro]]. [https://www.reuters.com/world/americas/lula-vows-defend-brazils-supreme-court-us-threatens-judge-2025-06-03/ (Reuters)]
*[[2025 United Nations Security Council election]]
**Bahrain, Colombia, the Democratic Republic of the Congo, Latvia, and Liberia are elected as non-permanent members of the [[United Nations Security Council]] for a two-year term. [https://www.reuters.com/world/americas/five-countries-elected-un-security-council-202627-2025-06-03/ (Reuters)]

'''Law and crime'''
*A female doctor was attacked and beaten up by a 45-year old man in [[Koszalin]], [[Poland]]. The woman was later hospitalized. Based on the information provided, police officers detained a 45-year-old man on a nearby street. At the time of his arrest, he continued to display aggression, so the decision was made to transport him to a specialist hospital for further observation and protection.[https://koszalininfo.pl/45-latek-napadl-na-lekarke-kobieta-trafila-do-szpitala/ (KoszalinInfo)]
*[[Fall of the Assad regime]]
**A court in [[Stuttgart]], [[Germany]], sentences a [[Syria]]n man to [[life in prison]] under [[universal jurisdiction]] for leading a [[Hezbollah]]-backed group and committing alleged [[war crimes]] against [[Sunni Muslims]] in [[Bosra|Busra al-Sham]], Syria, during the [[Syrian civil war]]. [https://www.dw.com/en/germany-jails-syrian-pro-assad-fighter-over-war-crimes/a-72776468 (DW)]
*[[Killing of Nahel Merzouk]]
**A [[France|French]] [[Law enforcement in France|police officer]] goes on trial after being charged with killing 17-year-old Nahel Merzouk on June 27, 2023, whose death sparked the [[Nahel Merzouk riots|riots]] across France and other [[Overseas France|French territories]]. [https://www.reuters.com/world/french-police-officer-go-trial-murder-teenager-2025-06-03/ (Reuters)]
*[[LGBTQ rights in Hungary]]
**[[Law enforcement in Hungary|Police]] in [[Hungary]] deny the request for permission to hold the [[Budapest Pride]] event, citing the recent [[2025 Hungarian Pride ban|ban]] by the [[Hungarian government]]. [https://apnews.com/article/hungary-budapest-police-reject-pride-march-2e8db9aedd57c9cf36f18f5a78708c62 (AP)]
*[[MI5#Domestic abuse scandal|MI5 domestic abuse scandal]]
**MI5 apologizes to the [[UK High Court]]s for providing false evidence in regards to an agent who abused their partner. [https://www.independent.co.uk/news/uk/crime/mi5-bbc-high-court-suella-braverman-london-b2762772.html (The Independent)] [https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/articles/c4ge87g2lngo (BBC News)]
*Two hundred and sixteen prisoners escape from a prison in the [[Malir District]], [[Pakistan]]. During the escape, which was a result of panic caused by an earthquake, one prisoner is killed and two prison officers are injured. A search operation is ongoing and 80 prisoners have been recaptured. [https://www.bbc.com/news/articles/cwyvwv0e55po (BBC News)]
*Nineteen prisoners, including eleven members of the armed group [[West Papua National Liberation Army]], escape from a prison in [[Nabire]], [[Central Papua]], [[Indonesia]]. Three prison staff were critically injured. A search around the city is ongoing. [https://www.tempo.co/hukum/kronologi-19-anggota-opm-kabur-setelah-bacok-sipir-lapas-nabire-1633149 (Tempo)]

'''Politics and elections'''
*[[2025 South Korean presidential election]]
**Citizens of [[South Korea]] vote in a [[snap election]] to elect their [[President of South Korea|president]] between five candidates. The election is held 60 days after [[Yoon Suk Yeol]] was [[Impeachment of Yoon Suk Yeol|ousted]] by the [[Constitutional Court of Korea]] six months after the failed [[2024 South Korean martial law crisis|declaration of martial law]]. [https://www.ft.com/content/814195d4-e5a0-40ef-b1a7-a3165192ecb9 (''Financial Times'')]
**[[Lee Jae-Myung]] of the [[Democratic Party (South Korea, 2015)|Democratic Party]] is elected the 14th [[president of South Korea]]. [https://en.yna.co.kr/view/AEN20250602004960315?section=national/politics (Yonhap News Agency)] [https://www.npr.org/2025/06/02/g-s1-70029/south-korea-presidential-elections (NPR)]
*[[Schoof cabinet]]
**The [[Party for Freedom]] withdraws from the current [[Cabinet of the Netherlands|Dutch cabinet]] after failing to come to an agreement with coalition partners over amending the [[Netherlands]]'s [[asylum seeker|asylum]] rules. [https://nltimes.nl/2025/06/03/dutch-cabinet-collapses-wilders-pulls-coalition-pvv-stalls-asylum-policy (NLTimes)]
**[[Prime Minister of the Netherlands|Prime Minister]] [[Dick Schoof]] announces his resignation. [https://www.theguardian.com/world/live/2025/jun/03/europe-live-dutch-netherlands-far-right-leader-geert-wilders-quits-ukraine-russia-poland (''The Guardian'')]
*[[2025 Mongolian protests]]
**[[Mongolia]]n [[Prime Minister of Mongolia|prime minister]] [[Luvsannamsrain Oyun-Erdene]] resigns after weeks of protests. [https://www.theguardian.com/world/2025/jun/03/mongolia-pm-resigns-luvsannamsrai-confidence-vote-protests (''The Guardian'')]
